hints: Every number from 1 to n becomes exactly one string in the list. Which case must you test first so that 15 does not turn into just "Tick"?
A single loop from 1 to n with an if / else-if chain on the remainder operator %. Test the 'both' case (divisible by 15) before the single cases, and add each string to a list you return at the end.

1. Create an empty list of strings.
  2. Loop i from 1 to n.
  3. If i % 15 == 0 add "TickTock".
  4. Else if i % 3 == 0 add "Tick".
  5. Else if i % 5 == 0 add "Tock".
  6. Else add i converted to a string.
  7. Return the list.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass from 1 to n, deciding each entry with the remainder checks in the right order.

explain: For n = 15 the list starts "1", "2", "Tick", "4", "Tock" and so on. At 15 both 3 and 5 divide it, so the first branch (i % 15 == 0) must catch it; if you tested % 3 first you would add "Tick" and never reach the combined case. The order of the if-chain is the whole trick. Plain numbers must be added as strings, e.g. String.valueOf(i) in Java.
recognize: Produce something different depending on which numbers divide i → a loop with an ordered if / else-if chain on %.
